id: P3 predicted population ledger, Domesday 1086 blind
status: frozen before the Domesday statistics database is opened (only the places database's column names and five place rows had been read)
question: Does the Earth-calibrated chain predict where people lived, and how many, in a long-settled low-input farming landscape? The atlas today spreads a supplied budget; this tests whether it can predict the total itself.

candidates.P0_capacity: people/km2 = the Earth harness capacity (scripts/land_people_earth.py, output/land_people/earth/earth.npz 'capacity': crops on arable from slope + D2/D2b irrigation, FALLOW 0.600 fitted so the North China Plain AD 2 census sits at capacity) - full occupation
candidates.P1_base: people/km2 = harvest.models settlement base x the central occupation share (polity.earth.earth_people) - the density the atlas allocates by; distribution only (its level is a share)
candidates.P2_cored: people/km2 = capacity x exp(-D / 800 km), D the travel cost to the nearest old core (Uruk, Memphis, Harappa, Zhengzhou, Rome; forest x2, relief +1 per km, sea as land; scripts/population_cores.py travel_distance, coarsen 3) - the Earth-tested occupancy rule (reports/POPULATION_20261023.md), level anchored at the North China Plain
candidates.fixed: no parameter is fitted on Domesday; foraging is taken as zero in England 1086 (fully farmed); towns are inside the recorded population

truth.places: data/cache/domesday/places_content.mdb (owner upload, sha256 6359d8b15b60caecd35de310c269dd2c461ddbc5b6a8dc4c4d041181346f0356): table Places, located by OSrefs (1-km Ordnance Survey reference; the centre of the square; British National Grid on OSGB36 converted to latitude/longitude, datum shift ignored at block scale); the first reference when several
truth.people: the statistics database's recorded population per holding (its total field if it has one, else the sum of all recorded person categories: villans, bordars, cottars, slaves, freemen, sokemen, burgesses and other recorded people; no livestock, ploughs or values), joined to places by the shared place key; a holding naming several places is split equally among them; holdings that cannot be joined are counted and reported, not imputed
truth.multiplier: none for the rank test; the level test compares with published totals instead

area_and_blocks.surveyed_mask: Earth-harness land cells (5 arc-min) within 15 km of a located Domesday place
area_and_blocks.blocks: British National Grid 20 km squares (by cell centre); a block counts if it has >= 4 land cells and >= 50 % of them in the mask; density = people / land km2 over its masked cells

metrics.R_rank: Spearman rank correlation between model and Domesday recorded density over the 20 km blocks (ties averaged); also the share of people that would have to move (half the L1 distance of normalized shares)
metrics.L_level: predicted people in the surveyed mask (P0 and P2) against the published range for England in 1086, 1.2-2.6 M (lower estimates multiply the ~269,000 recorded heads by 4-5; upper about 2.25-2.5 M; Broadberry et al. 2015 central 1.71 M); score |ln(predicted / 1.71 M)|. The total is common knowledge, so this part is semi-blind; the block pattern is the unseen part

gates.R: a candidate's distribution counts as Earth-tested at the 20 km block scale if its Spearman >= 0.30
gates.L: a candidate's predicted level counts as Earth-tested (one region) if its total is inside 1.2-2.6 M
gates.atlas: if P2 passes R and L, the atlas population layer gets a predicted-total mode on the map (capacity x the lore-core occupancy, unnormalized) next to the supplied budget, badged by this result; otherwise the supplied budget stays and the result is reported with the badges updated

development_seen: report only, nothing selected: Han AD 2 commandery Spearman for P0/P1/P2 on the current harness (published: base 0.29, cored travel 0.84) and the ten-region RMS of ln(historical / predicted) for P0 and P2
step2_note: village-scale settlement (Step 2) is not scored here: the atlas has no village generator yet and no development village pool. After this scoring Domesday counts as seen for any later village test.
